meta.title: Slova — words and grammar
meta.description: Paste English words and study them. Grammar courses explain a rule, then drill it.
meta.ogTitle: Slova — paste a word list, learn the grammar
meta.ogDescription: Translations fill in from a shared dictionary of more than 8,000 words. Seven practice formats and grammar courses.

landing.heroBody: Type or paste words — the translations fill in by themselves. Grammar courses explain a rule and hand it straight back as practice. Come back when the words are due.
landing.statLexicon: words in the shared dictionary — translated, with recorded pronunciation
landing.statFormats: question formats for one word, from recognising it to writing it
landing.statRequest: for the whole list instead of forty — and most of the time, none at all
landing.stepPasteBody: Type or paste English words. Translations fill in as you add them.
landing.stepStudyBody: One card, seven formats. Recognising a word is easy; writing it is not.
landing.stepRuleBody: A grammar course: the rule on a card, then the drill. Present Simple is first.
landing.stepDueBody: The schedule brings the words back. Nothing to organise by hand.
landing.dictionaryTitle: Paste — and the translations are there.
landing.dictionaryBody: Type or paste. Most words come from a shared dictionary that already exists, with audio recorded. Only what is missing from it goes to a model — once.
landing.practiceBody: Recognise it, hear it, write it. The same word comes back from a different side each time — and the whole drill works from the keyboard.
landing.coursesTitle: A rule, and the drill right behind it.
landing.coursesBody: Longer than a training, shorter than a textbook. Every lesson shows the rule and then asks you to use it. Present Simple is first — six lessons, from forms to a test.
landing.closeTitle: Start with a list — or open a course.
landing.closeBody: Your first forty words will be translated before you finish reading this line.

product.todayBody: A short session now keeps them sticky.

legal.privacyMetaDescription: What Slova stores, who sees it, and how to ask for it to be deleted.
legal.privacyDescription: What we keep in order to run the app, and nothing else.
legal.whoBody: Slova is the vocabulary app at slova.study. There is no separate company behind the name. Questions: <email></email>.
legal.store1: Your email, and a password hash if you set one. We never store the password itself.
legal.store2: Your name and photo, if you sign in with Google.
legal.store3: The words you add, your translations, sets, and study schedule.
legal.store4: Where you are in a grammar course, if you take one.
legal.else1: Neon holds the database. Vercel hosts the app.
legal.else2: Resend sends the confirmation and password-reset emails.
legal.else3: Google, if you use Google to sign in.
legal.else4: Anthropic, when a word you pasted is not already in the shared dictionary — so it can be translated. A translation you type stays private until a second source agrees with it.
legal.else5: Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights count visits. They do not get your word lists.
legal.cookiesBody: A session cookie keeps you signed in. A language cookie remembers English or Russian. Those are the only cookies we set on purpose.
legal.howLongBody: We keep the account until you ask us to delete it. Write to <email></email> and we will remove your row and the words attached to it.
legal.childrenBody: Slova is not aimed at children under 16. If an account was created for someone younger, write and we will delete it.
legal.termsMetaDescription: How you may use Slova, and what the app does not promise.
legal.termsDescription: A small app. A short agreement.
legal.theAppBody: Slova helps you learn English words with Russian translations. You paste a list or take a grammar course, then come back when words are due. Use it for yourself. Do not use it to break the law or to abuse the translation budget.
legal.yourWordsBody: Lists you add belong to you. We may keep a translation in a shared dictionary so the next person does not pay for the same word — only after a second independent source agrees with it, so a typo does not spread. The frequency list used to seed that dictionary has its own licence; see the notice on the site if that matters to you.
legal.accountsBody: You are responsible for the email and password you use to sign in. We can close an account that is harming the service. You can ask us to close yours: <email></email>.
legal.warrantyBody: The app is provided as it is. Translations can be wrong. Study schedules are a guess. We are not liable for what you do with either.
legal.rightsIntro: Write to <email></email> and we will do any of these.
legal.rights1: Show you what we hold. Most of it is already on screen.
legal.rights2: Send you your words as a file — the list with translations, sets and schedule.
legal.rights4: Delete the account, and the words with it. That one does not come back.
legal.whereBody: The database is Neon, in AWS us-east-1 — Virginia, in the United States. The app runs on Vercel, also in the United States, and their nodes serve the static files worldwide. Mail goes through Resend. If you are in Europe: your data leaves the EU, and creating an account is how you agree to that.
